title: Training options
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T14:55:58Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank points focus on training versus development, with on-the-job and off-the-job only as supporting definitions, so neither teaches the pros and cons of each training option as the new point does.

draft.title: Training options
card: training that happens at the workplace while the employee does real work, such as shadowing a colleague or being coached by a supervisor.
training that happens away from the normal work task, such as a course at a TAFE, a workshop or an online program.
On-the-job training is usually cheaper and relevant to the actual job. It can be uneven, because the quality depends on the trainer, and mistakes can happen on real work.
Off-the-job training can teach new skills and ideas from experts, without the pressure of real work. It often costs more, and the employee is away from their duties while they learn.
draft.remember: On-the-job is learning while working. Off-the-job is learning away from the task. Each trades cost and relevance against expert teaching.

a.q: Ravi starts at a bakery in Ballarat. For his first week he works beside an experienced baker and copies how she shapes loaves. What type of training is this?
a.why: Ravi learns while doing real work at the bakery, so it is on-the-job training. It is not off-the-job, because he has not left the work setting to learn in a class or workshop.
a.clue: Where is Ravi while he learns?

b.q: Priya owns a small accounting firm in Geelong. She sends two staff to a two-day workshop run by experts on new tax software. What is a likely disadvantage of this choice?
opts: The staff are away from client work while they learn
The training is limited to what a supervisor knows
The staff may make costly mistakes on live client work
The training is less relevant to any job tasks
b.why: A workshop is off-the-job training, so the staff are away from their duties, which costs the firm time and money. Mistakes on live work and reliance on one supervisor are risks of on-the-job training, which is the tempting wrong choice here.
b.clue: Think about where the staff are while the workshop runs.

b.best: The staff are away from client work while they learn
